citations.quote: Study ALN-AS1-003 (ENVISION (Study 003)) was the pivotal study to establish the efficacy and safety of givosiran and upon which the application was based.

ALN-AS1-003 (ENVISION; Study 003 (NCT03338816)): Phase 3 Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-Controlled Multicenter Study with an Open-label Extension to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Givosiran in Patients with Acute Hepatic Porphyrias.

It was a Phase 3, randomized (1:1), multicenter, double-blind (DB), placebo-controlled study to assess the efficacy and safety of subcutaneously administered givosiran in patients \ge 12 years with documented diagnosis of acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) and any non-AIP acute hepatic porphyria (AHP), which includes hereditary coproporphyria (HCP), variegated porphyria (VP), and aminolevulinic acid (ALA) dehydratase deficient porphyria (ADP).

design.text: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with a 6-month double-blind period and an open-label extension.

citations.quote: It was a Phase 3, randomized (1:1), multicenter, double-blind (DB), placebo-controlled study to assess the efficacy and safety of subcutaneously administered givosiran in patients \ge 12 years with documented diagnosis of acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) and any non-AIP acute hepatic porphyria (AHP), which includes hereditary coproporphyria (HCP), variegated porphyria (VP), and aminolevulinic acid (ALA) dehydratase deficient porphyria (ADP).

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: annualized rate of porphyria attacks (AAR) requiring hospitalization, urgent care visit, or in-home IV hemin administration, in AIP patients.

citations.quote: **Primary.** The primary endpoint was the annualized rate of porphyria attacks (AAR) that require hospitalization, urgent care visit, or in-home IV hemin administration.

n.text: 94 AHP patients randomized (48 givosiran, 46 placebo); 89 were AIP (primary analysis set).

citations.quote: Due to rapid enrollment, the actual number of AHP patients randomized was 94, 89 of whom were AIP.

result.text: Study met its primary endpoint: annualized AAR 3.9 with givosiran vs 14.3 with placebo; patients on givosiran experienced 70% (95% CI 53%, 84%) fewer attacks (rate ratio 0.27; 95% CI 0.16, 0.47).

citations.quote: Givosiran arm was approximately 1.8 (95% CI: 1.2, 2.7) attacks per person, or roughly 3.9 (95% CI: 2.6, 5.8) attacks on an annualized basis.
Placebo arm was approximately 6.6 (95% CI: 4.5, 9.5) attacks per person, or roughly 14.3 (95% CI: 9.9, 20.7) attacks on an annualized basis.
The efficacy data suggested that patients in the givosiran arm experienced 70% (95% CI: 53%, 84%) fewer porphyria attacks than patients in the placebo arm.
